reflections.title: Clean Hands for Holy Things

reflect.text: In Israel, the priests were not allowed to touch or eat the sacred food if they were unclean. Approaching God's consecrated offerings in a defiled state risked judgment and separation from His presence. God does not accept religious service, gifts, or worship when we hold onto sin. As F. B. Meyer noted, we should seek cleansing before we take part in holy things. Before we open the Scriptures, join in church worship, or come to the Lord's Supper, we need to ask Christ to wash our hearts clean.

The law also made clear who could sit at the priest's table. Strangers and hired workers were kept away, but anyone bought with the priest's money or born into his household could freely eat. Charles Spurgeon explains that our great High Priest, Jesus Christ, has bought us with a price and caused us to be born into God's family. Because we belong to Christ, we share in His peace and joy. At the same time, we are called to guard our minds and conduct, walking each day in faithful obedience to Him.

questions: Are there attitudes or actions you need to bring to Jesus for cleansing before you worship or read His Word?
How does knowing you are bought by Christ and born into His family encourage you to walk in obedience?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for buying us with Your own blood and welcoming us into Your household. Forgive our sins and cleanse our hearts so that our worship and service are pleasing to You. Help us to guard our minds and walk faithfully in Your presence today. Amen.
